Editable PowerPoint output via officer

Source: R/dml.R
as_dml.Rd

Put a scene on a PowerPoint slide as editable shapes: every mark is a DrawingML freeform (or a preset rectangle or ellipse), every label a real text box whose words can be retyped, and each panel a named group that can be ungrouped, recoloured or moved in PowerPoint.

Usage

as_dml(x, text = c("native", "outline"), resize = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A vl_scene(), or anything with an as_vellum_scene() method.

text

"native" (default) for editable text runs, "outline" for glyph outlines.

resize

Re-solve the layout at the location's size (default TRUE).

Value

as_dml(): a vellum_dml object, for officer::ph_with().

Details

With the officer package installed, a scene goes straight into officer::ph_with(); as_dml() wraps anything else as_vellum_scene() can compile (a vellumplot plot, say) so it can go there too:

doc <- officer::read_pptx()
doc <- officer::add_slide(doc, layout = "Title and Content")
doc <- officer::ph_with(doc, scene, location = officer::ph_location_type("body"))
doc <- officer::ph_with(doc, as_dml(plot), location = officer::ph_location_fullsize())
print(doc, target = "deck.pptx")

To write a deck without officer, give render() a .pptx path (one slide) or use pptx_pages() (several).

Size

By default the scene is laid out again at the size of the location (resize = TRUE), exactly as render() would at that size, so text keeps its point size and nothing is stretched. resize = FALSE keeps the scene's own size, anchored at the location's top-left corner.

Text and fonts

Each label names the font vellum measured it with. PowerPoint uses that font when the machine opening the deck has it and substitutes another when it does not; the box is anchored so a wider substitute grows away from the label's anchor (right-aligned tick labels stay right-aligned) rather than drifting. Fonts are not embedded. text = "outline" writes glyph outlines instead: identical everywhere, but no longer editable as text. An md() label is one text run per styled span (bold, italic, colour; a superscript or subscript as a raised or lowered run). tex() labels, md() labels with inline math, halos and text set on a path are always outlines, as in SVG.

What cannot be expressed

DrawingML has no clipping, blend modes, masks or group opacity.

  • Clipped geometry is cut in advance: fills to the visible area, strokes along their centreline (a round or square cap at a cut end reaches half a line width past the edge), pictures cropped. Native text cannot be cut: a label crossing a clip edge is drawn whole, with a warning (outlined text is cut exactly).

  • Group opacity over shapes that do not overlap is folded into their colours, which is exactly what the group composites to.

  • Blend modes, masks, blur and shadow effects, and group opacity over overlapping shapes are drawn as a picture of the region they cover, with a warning: the slide looks right, but that part is not editable.

  • Linear and radial gradients are native gradient fills, patterns a tiled picture fill. A radial gradient's focal point moves to its centre (with a warning). Rasters become pictures.

LibreOffice is not a reliable preview for these: it drops gradients with translucent stops and the transparency of tiled pattern pictures, and places an off-centre radial gradient differently.

For charts whose data stays editable in PowerPoint, see the mschart package; this writes the drawing, not the data.

See also

render() and pptx_pages() to write a .pptx without officer.

Examples

sc <- vl_scene(6, 4, dpi = 96, bg = "white") |>
  draw(rect_grob(width = 0.5, height = 0.5, gp = vl_gpar(fill = "tomato"))) |>
  draw(text_grob("editable", gp = vl_gpar(fontsize = 24)))
doc <- officer::read_pptx()
doc <- officer::add_slide(doc, layout = "Blank", master = "Office Theme")
doc <- officer::ph_with(doc, as_dml(sc),
  location = officer::ph_location(left = 1, top = 1, width = 6, height = 4)
)
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".pptx")
print(doc, target = f)
